Article Title: Apple ‘Welcome Home’ event today: HomePod mini, Apple TV and other products expected to launch
Article Text:
Apple HomeView is expected at the Welcome Home event on October 13

Apple’s new smart home hub could get a screen

HomePod mini may get S11 chip

New Apple TV could focus on performance

Apple is all set to hold its ‘Welcome Home’ launch event today (October 13). Apple confirmed the event last week through a teaser shared by its marketing chief Greg Joswiak, with the tagline strongly hinting at a major push into the smart home category. At the event, the company is expected to unveil its “long-awaited smart home hub with a screen, the new HomePod mini and an updated Apple TV,” Gurman stated. All three devices will have Siri AI at the core, he added. This will be the company’s first event after the September event where it unveiled 2026 iPhone lineup – iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, along with iPhone Duo. Apple’s October 13 event could mark a major push into smart home devices. Here’s what to expect.The most notable launch is expected to be a new smart home hub with a built-in display, which could compete with devices such as Google Nest Hub and Amazon Echo Show. The device is rumoured to feature an S11 chip, which could support faster performance and Siri AI features. The screen could be used to show information such as weather updates, calendar events and music controls.A FaceTime camera is also among the expected features, potentially allowing the device to double as a video-calling hub.Apple is also reportedly developing a specialised operating system for the device focused on smart home controls.Apple is also expected to introduce an updated HomePod mini. The overall design may remain largely unchanged, while an upgraded S11 chip could improve performance and Siri responsiveness. The speaker could also get tighter integration with Apple’s smart home ecosystem and potentially new colour options.The third expected launch is an updated Apple TV. The device is rumoured to receive a more powerful chip, potentially the A19 or A19 Pro, which could improve gaming, streaming and multitasking. The updated Apple TV could also feature deeper Siri AI integration for voice-controlled navigation and smart home functions. Other possible additions include HDMI pass-through and a redesigned Siri Remote.All three devices are expected to have Siri AI at the core, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, making the October event potentially important for Apple’s wider smart home strategy.
Article Summary: Apple is expected to unveil its ‘long-awaited smart home hub with a screen, the new HomePod mini and an updated Apple TV’ All three devices are expected to have Siri AI at the core, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman. Apple confirmed the event last week through a teaser.

Article Title: Architect Andrew Batey designed this 1972 glass house for a photographer; the Berkeley Hills home with a former darkroom is listed for $1.088 million
Article Text:
Image: Left/Harry Bowles (Credit: Manitoba Historical Society Archives)/Right/Matt Harper/NorCalHomeTours

Andrew Batey designed the Berkeley glass house for photographer Henry Bowles

The two-storey glass façade brings Berkeley’s woodland into the home

"The Photographer's House,” at 141 Fairlawn Dr. in Berkeley (Image: Matt Harper/NorCalHomeTours)

A floating staircase, loft bedroom and skylit bathroom shape the interior

The former darkroom adds a creative legacy to the $1.088 million listing

A glass house nestled among the trees of California’s Berkeley Hills is attracting attention for its unusual architecture and creative history. Designed in 1972 by architect Andrew Batey for architectural photographer Henry Bowles, the residence was conceived to connect its interiors with the surrounding woodland. The two-bedroom property combines glass, steel and redwood in a design that makes natural light and the landscape central to its character. Now listed for $1.088 million, the home is being offered after more than two decades under its current owner. Its former photographic darkroom, double-height living room and distinctive glass façade add to its appeal.The story of the Photographer’s House began in 1972, when architectural photographer Henry Bowles commissioned a residence that reflected his appreciation for design and natural light. According to SFGATE, Bowles had trained under renowned Western photographer Morley Baer before establishing his own professional reputation. Architect Andrew Batey, who was 28 when he undertook the project, designed the house using glass, steel and redwood. The commission brought together Bowles’s interest in architectural photography and Batey’s developing modernist approach. The residence is identified as one of Batey’s early commissions, predating his subsequent work with architect Mark Mack at the firm Batey and Mack.The house therefore offers a glimpse into the architect’s early career while preserving the creative vision behind its original commission.The property’s defining feature is its expansive glass façade, which creates a visual connection between the interior and the wooded hillside outside. According to the New York Post, the 1,625-square-foot house combines glass, steel and redwood to create a distinctive modernist residence. Its double-height living room gives the relatively compact home a sense of openness, while sliding glass doors lead towards a spacious deck. Realtor also highlighted the two-storey glass wall as a defining feature of the property, helping explain its appeal to readers interested in distinctive homes. Rather than placing conventional walls between residents and the landscape, the design allows trees and daylight to become part of the visual experience. The combination of exposed structural elements and extensive glazing gives the house a character that remains closely tied to its woodland setting.Inside, the Photographer’s House combines an open layout with architectural details that distinguish it from a conventional two-bedroom residence. SFGATE describes a double-height living area with exposed beams, alongside an updated kitchen featuring quartz countertops and custom honeycomb tile. A floating staircase with cable railing connects the main living space to the upper level, where a 400-square-foot mezzanine accommodates the second bedroom among the oak treetops. The primary suite has its own entrance, adding a degree of separation within the home’s open design. Another notable feature is the black-tiled bathroom, illuminated by two skylights. Batey returned in the late 1980s to design the bathroom, extending his involvement with the property beyond its original construction. These details combine contemporary updates with the architectural character of the original house.The property’s history as a photographer’s residence extends beyond its main living spaces. Batey originally built a darkroom beside the single-car garage, providing Bowles with a dedicated space for photographic work. The approximately 300-square-foot area now features a skylight and offers potential for use as a studio, guest space or home office. The current owner, Mike Moye, discovered the property in 2003 after a photograph of its glass façade caught his attention. He subsequently spent more than two decades living in and updating the residence, including improvements to the kitchen and outdoor areas. Realtor reported that the property became the most popular home on its weekly list, demonstrating the online interest generated by its unusual design. Listed for $1.088 million, the Berkeley Hills house brings together architectural history, woodland views and adaptable creative space.
Article Summary: The Photographer’s House was designed in 1972 by architect Andrew Batey for architectural photographer Henry Bowles. The two-bedroom property combines glass, steel and redwood in a design that makes natural light and the landscape central to its character. The home is being offered after more than two decades under its current owner.

Article Title: Britain built a 70-foot water tower disguised as a house in 1923; its 50,000-gallon tank was damaged by a wartime shell before the landmark became a holiday home
Article Text:
Representative Image of Thorpeness’s whimsical house-shaped water tower surrounded by trees in Suffolk ( AI Generrated Image)

House in the Clouds: how Thorpeness disguised a water tower

Wartime damage changed the water tower’s capacity

From water infrastructure to holiday accommodation

In the English village of Thorpeness, a 70-foot structure built to store water was designed to resemble a house perched above the trees. Completed in 1923, the building concealed a tank with an original capacity of 50,000 gallons, while the structure below provided living accommodation. Known as the House in the Clouds, it was part of the development of Thorpeness, a planned holiday village on the Suffolk coast. Glencairn Stuart Ogilvie, the owner and developer of the Thorpeness Estate, conceived the village and commissioned architects to help realise its distinctive design. Historic England credits Frederick Forbes Glennie with the building’s 1923 design, commissioned as part of Glencairn Stuart Ogilvie’s development of Thorpeness. Its timber weatherboarding, gabled roof and domestic-style windows helped it fit the village’s unusual architectural character. More than a century later, the building remains a landmark, despite no longer serving its original purpose as a water tower.The House in the Clouds was built to provide a water supply for Thorpeness. Its unusual appearance reflected the character of the village, which Ogilvie developed as a holiday destination with buildings designed to create a distinctive landscape rather than a conventional resort.The building’s Historic England listing describes a steel-frame structure clad in weatherboarding, topped by a pantiled, gabled roof. The lower part consists of a five-storey tower, while the upper section, supported by arched corner braces, housed the water tank. Windows were incorporated into the structure, including casement windows and projecting bay windows.The original tank held 50,000 gallons. According to the property’s official history, water was pumped from a well using the neighbouring windmill, with a petrol engine available as an alternative when wind conditions were insufficient. The elevated tank formed part of the water-supply system developed for the village. The building was initially called the Gazebo. Mrs Malcolm Mason, a children’s author and friend of Ogilvie, christened it the House in the Clouds. The property’s history records that a poem she wrote in 1923 was inspired by the building. Its new name captured the appearance of a house seemingly suspended above the surrounding trees. Historic England, which designated the building Grade II listed in 1995, describes it as a landmark and the best-known building in the resort village. Its combination of domestic architecture and water-storage infrastructure has helped preserve its distinctive identity.The building was damaged during the Second World War. According to the property’s official history, an English Bofors anti-aircraft shell passed through the tank’s south-eastern corner in 1943 while the gun was firing at a V1 flying bomb. The shell damaged the tank, and two women, the Miss Humphreys, were occupying the accommodation below and were asleep at the time. The subsequent repairs reduced the tank’s capacity from 50,000 gallons to 30,000 gallons. The property’s history records that sections of the tank’s existing steel were used in the repair. The reduction meant that the tower could hold 20,000 fewer gallons than it had originally been designed to store.The building’s water-supply arrangements also evolved over the following decades. An electric pump replaced the petrol engine in 1953, according to the property’s history. By 1963, a wider water supply had been introduced to the area, although the tank continued to be used for storage for a period afterwards. The tower eventually ceased to serve its original function. The property’s history places the end of its use for local water storage in 1977. The tank itself was removed in 1979, opening the way for the former storage space to become part of the house. Refurbishment of the interior and restoration of the garden began in 1987. These changes allowed the structure to survive beyond the purpose for which it had been built. Rather than remaining a working water tower, it became a house whose unusual upper section no longer needed to accommodate a large volume of water.Today, the House in the Clouds operates as holiday accommodation. Its official accommodation page lists five bedrooms distributed across the second, third and fourth floors, with a games room on the fifth floor. The different levels allow guests to experience a building whose layout developed from its original combination of a water tank and living space. The property stands on Uplands Road in Thorpeness, in Suffolk, close to the village’s golf course and Meare, the artificial lake created as part of the resort’s development. Visitors can find practical details through the property’s official location page.The building’s appeal comes from the contrast between its appearance and its original function. From a distance, its roof and weatherboarded exterior resemble a house elevated above the village. Its history, however, is tied to a practical need: storing and supplying water to the developing community. The House in the Clouds is an example of how infrastructure can become part of a place’s architectural identity. Built in 1923, damaged during wartime, altered when its water-storage role ended, and later adapted for holiday use, it has remained a recognisable feature of Thorpeness. Its original purpose has disappeared, but the structure continues to serve a new one while retaining the appearance that made it unusual in the first place.
Article Summary: The House in the Clouds was part of the development of Thorpeness, a planned holiday village on the Suffolk coast. Completed in 1923, the building concealed a tank with an original capacity of 50,000 gallons, while the structure below provided living accommodation. The structure was damaged during the Second World War.

Article Title: In Kenya, engineers added blue-gum wood ash to weak road-base soil; the mix achieved a 348% bearing score, over twice the 160% design requirement
Article Text:
AI-generated representative image showing blue-gum wood ash being blended with cement and reddish lateritic soil for road-base material testing in Kenya. Credits - Gemini

Eucalyptus globulus

How wood ashes were used

The significance of the 348% result

Why the ash could help

AI-generated representative image showing a California Bearing Ratio test used to evaluate the bearing resistance of cement- and wood-ash-stabilised soil. Credits - Gemini

Limits of the lab results

Weak soil can make road construction more difficult, so engineers often use cement to strengthen road-base material. In a 2021 laboratory study, Blaise Dabou, Christopher Kanali and Zachary Abiero-Gariy investigated whether ash from blue gum trees () could replace part of the cement used to stabilize lateritic soil. The researchers reported a peak soaked California Bearing Ratio (CBR) of 348% for a mixture containing 4% cement and 2% blue-gum wood ash by weight of soil. The result exceeded the 160% road-base benchmark cited from Kenya’s Road Design Manual.Lateritic soil develops in warm regions after extended weathering and is generally rich in iron and aluminium oxides, which give it a reddish or brown colour. Its engineering qualities exhibit significant location-dependent variation. Some lateritic soils are suitable for use in road building, whereas some need to be treated to provide the strength required for a pavement base. The researchers first tested the soil with Portland cement at levels ranging from 0% to 12% by weight of soil. They determined the California bearing ratio and unconfined compressive strength to select a cement-only mix that would be appropriate for subsequent testing.The mixture containing 6% cement recorded an unconfined compressive strength of 2.88 megapascals after seven days of curing. The researchers then wondered whether they might substitute some of the cement with blue gum wood ash while still making the material work as a road base.In the investigation on lateritic soil stabilised with cement and blue gum wood ash, the levels of replacement utilising the ash were investigated in incremental values.The optimum CBR was obtained at 2% blue gum wood ash. For the best effect, the ash replaced some of the original cement in the mix and was not the only stabilising material.The soaking CBR of the combination with 4% cement and 2% blue gum wood ash was 348%. The unconfined compressive strength value after 7 days of curing was reported to be 2.99 megapascals. The CBR value of the cement- or lime-improved foundation material from Kenya’s Road Design Manual was compared with the benchmark of 160%.The California Bearing Ratio (CBR) test measures a soil or pavement material’s resistance to penetration relative to a standard crushed-rock reference material. Results are conventionally expressed as percentages, and values can exceed 100%. Therefore, the reported CBR of 348% is a penetration-resistance ratio, not a claim that the soil is 348% as strong or that a road built with it would last more than twice as long. This information enables road engineers to evaluate whether a material can resist the stresses anticipated in a pavement layer. The test must be read in conjunction with the curing conditions, moisture, soil properties and other strength values.The Ministry of Roads and Transport in Kenya has a manual on materials and pavement design that provides guidance on the use of soil classifications and material testing for constructing road structures. Such parameters are important since a laboratory value is only of practical importance if the test technique and material type are compatible with the specifications of the pavement which is intended to be built.Wood ash is a mineral compound. The chemical composition is dependent on the tree type, burning circumstances of the wood, and the collection and treatment of the ash. When coupled with cement and soil, adequate ash particles and chemical elements can impact the compacted structure and the processes that occur during curing.The researchers found that a mix containing 4% cement and 2% wood ash achieved a seven-day compressive strength of 2.99 MPa, slightly higher than the 2.88 MPa recorded for the 6% cement-only mix. The combined mixture retained the same total additive content by weight of soil while replacing two percentage points of cement with wood ash. Before it could be used in a road project, engineers would have to examine its chemistry, particle size and consistency. Also, the soil itself has to be tested, because the same stabiliser can give different outcomes in different ground conditions.The experiment was conducted on prepared soil samples under controlled settings. Moisture changes, traffic loading, drainage conditions, and quality of construction would affect field pavement. In the best-performing mixture, cement was still an essential part of the stabilising mechanism. Construction standards would also need to include appropriate mixing, compaction and curing techniques.The findings suggest that blue-gum wood ash may be useful as a partial cement replacement in lateritic road-base material. However, the results came from laboratory tests; field trials would be needed to determine how the mixture performs under real traffic, changing moisture conditions and long-term weather exposure.
Article Summary: Researchers in Kenya tested cement and blue gum wood ash in lateritic soil. They found a peak soaked California Bearing Ratio (CBR) of 348% for a mixture containing 4% cement and 2% blue-gum wood ash by weight of soil. The result exceeded the 160% road-base benchmark cited from Kenya’s Road Design Manual.

Article Title: TikTok star Becca Bloom teases never-before-shared personal stories ahead of January 2027 podcast launch
Article Text:
TikTok star Becca Bloom reveals what fans can expect from ‘Bloom's Room’

TikTok star Becca Bloom joins Pave Studios’ growing podcast lineup

TikTok star Becca Bloom is preparing to give fans a closer look at the person behind her popular online persona. The social media creator, who has built a following of more than 10 million across platforms, is stepping into long-form entertainment with a new podcast called “Bloom's Room. ” The weekly audio and video series will premiere in January 2027 under Pave Studios’ OpenMind lifestyle brand. Known for discussing money, fashion, relationships and business, Bloom now plans to explore these subjects in greater depth, sharing personal experiences and conversations that go beyond the short clips her audience knows.Bloom has built her online presence by discussing topics that affect everyday decisions, from financial goals to personal relationships. Her upcoming podcast will give her more room to explore these subjects, along with ambition, identity, investing and the psychology behind people's choices.The creator says the new project will also offer a different perspective on her private life. Although millions follow her online, she believes her short videos reveal only a small part of who she is."I'm a relatively private person, and what I've shared online has mostly been 30-second glimpses into my life.If those are the trailers, then 'Bloom's Room' is the movie," Bloom says.She also explained why she wanted to move beyond short-form content and create a space for longer discussions."The things I have the most to say about, and the conversations I think are actually worth having, rarely fit into 30 seconds," Bloom says. "We'll get into money, relationships, fashion, and why we make the choices we do, but also parts of my life and conversations I've never shared publicly."Each episode will focus on a subject Bloom wants to examine more closely. Some installments will draw on her finance background and experience building an online audience, while others will feature guests sharing their knowledge and personal stories.The format could allow Bloom to connect with viewers interested in more than quick advice or glimpses of her lifestyle. It will also give her the opportunity to discuss the difference between earning money and building ownership, alongside the challenges that can come with success.Pave Studios is expanding its creator-led programming by partnering with personalities who already have established audiences. The company plans to develop “Bloom's Room” across both audio and video, giving the series a wider format than traditional podcast listening alone.CEO Max Cutler welcomed the partnership, highlighting Bloom's appeal and the audience's interest in learning more about her life beyond social media.“Becca is one of the most compelling voices of her generation, and we’re thrilled to partner with her,” CEO Max Cutler says. “Her audience has always wanted to know more about the person behind the content, and this show creates the space for that. It’s exactly the kind of creator-led original OpenMind was built for, and we can’t wait for people to hear the conversations she’s going to have.”The January 2027 launch will add to OpenMind's growing slate, which includes “Khloé in Wonder Land,” hosted by Khloé Kardashian. Pave Studios also operates Crime House, which focuses on true crime, and Rewind, a history-focused brand.For Bloom, the new series marks a shift from brief social media updates to deeper conversations. Whether discussing financial decisions, relationships or personal ambition, she will have a new platform to share ideas that need more than a few seconds to explain.
Article Summary: TikTok star Becca Bloom is stepping into long-form entertainment with a new podcast. The weekly audio and video series will premiere in January 2027. Known for discussing money, fashion, relationships and business, Bloom now plans to explore these subjects in greater depth.

Article Title: Prince William's charitable foundation funded homes on Duchy land in Cornwall; in August, the first phase was handed to a charity, providing accommodation and support for 16 people facing homelessness
Article Text:
As the first residents prepare to move in, the project represents the Duchy of Cornwall’s first housing development specifically designed to address homelessness.

A new beginning in Nansledan

Housing with support at its core

Designed for a lower-carbon future

Poll Vote & Share your view What aspect of the Nansledan project do you find most important? Sustainable building materials Long-term stability for residents 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

A wider community taking shape

A new housing project in Cornwall is putting a different face on the fight against homelessness. Rather than treating shelter as a temporary stopgap, the development in Nansledan, Newquay, combines carefully designed homes with practical support, creating a more secure route towards independent living for people who have experienced homelessness. Scroll down to read the details.According to the Nansledan website, on August 4, 2026, St Petrocs received the keys to the first phase of the development from the Duchy of Cornwall. Funded by The Duke of Cornwall’s Charitable Foundation and built on Duchy-owned land, the scheme will provide accommodation for 16 people across two four-bedroom homes and eight one-bedroom apartments.Built by CG Fry & Son, the development was designed around more than simply providing a roof. On-site counselling space will allow St Petrocs to offer residents support alongside their accommodation, helping them establish greater stability as they work towards securing permanent housing, adds the report. The handover marks the completion of the construction phase and the beginning of the homes’ next chapter, with residents set to move into fully equipped properties, the report adds.The project forms part of Homewards, The Royal Foundation’s five-year programme established by The Duke of Cornwall with the ambition of demonstrating that homelessness can be prevented and made rare, brief and unrepeated.The programme brought the Duchy together with homelessness prevention specialists and people with lived experience, helping shape the design and approach to the development. The result is a model that places housing, wellbeing and community connection on the same footing.For St Petrocs, which supports people experiencing homelessness in Cornwall, the homes offer a chance to provide continuity rather than short-term intervention. Residents will have access to personalised support while becoming part of the wider Nansledan community.As per the report, sustainability is another defining feature of the project. The all-electric homes have been constructed with a focus on reducing both embodied carbon and the emissions associated with everyday use. Ultra-low-carbon cement and blockwork, super-insulated hemp-filled wall panels and solar panels form part of the environmental strategy. The approach is intended not only to reduce the development’s impact but also to keep future running costs lower for St Petrocs.The homes have also been furnished through the Homewards Furniture Project, with support from retailers and partners including Howdens, IKEA, DFS, B&Q, Bosch Home Appliances and Gordon Brown’s The Multibank charity. Sofas, tables, chairs, white goods and fitted kitchens mean residents can move into spaces that are ready to live in from day one.Nansledan itself reflects the Duchy’s broader approach to sustainable development. The urban extension to Newquay combines homes with shops, businesses, community facilities, green spaces and walkable neighbourhoods. The supported housing scheme adds another dimension to that vision: ensuring that those at risk of being left on the margins can also find a place within a growing community.As the first residents prepare to move in, the project represents the Duchy of Cornwall’s first housing development specifically designed to address homelessness. Its significance lies not just in the number of homes created, but in the idea behind them: that secure accommodation, meaningful support and a sense of belonging can work together to help people rebuild their lives.Images Courtesy: BBC and Royal Foundation
Article Summary: Nansledan, Newquay, is the Duchy of Cornwall’s first housing development specifically designed to address homelessness. The scheme will provide accommodation for 16 people across two four-bedroom homes and eight one-bedroom apartments. On-site counselling space will allow St Petrocs to offer residents support alongside their accommodation.

Article Title: Florida artists transformed their home into a mosaic wonderland using broken objects, discarded watch parts and computer circuit boards
Article Text:
PC: Mosaic House of Dunedin

How the artists turned their Florida home into a mosaic artwork

PC: Mosaic House of Dunedin

Carol Sackman uses discarded objects to create unexpected designs

Blake White developed his mosaic skills through experimentation

The artists believe creativity should be part of everyday life

Artists in Dunedin, Florida, have spent more than two decades transforming their home into a colourful mosaic artwork. Carol Sackman and Blake White purchased the house in 2000 and started decorating it with mosaics in 2003. Since then, their creations have spread across much of the kitchen, bathrooms, back garden fence and the sides of the house.According to the Mosaic House of Dunedin, their artwork also features in a sculpted mailbox and an eight-foot-by-eight-foot mosaic arch in the front yard. Sackman and White make some pieces individually and collaborate on others, bringing their distinct artistic approaches together. Their home reflects their shared belief in creative freedom and their desire to shape their surroundings through art.Carol Sackman and Blake White purchased the house in 2000 and began decorating it with mosaics in 2003. Over the years, their artwork has spread across much of the kitchen, bathrooms, back garden fence and the sides of the house. Their creations also feature a sculpted mailbox and an eight-foot-by-eight-foot mosaic arch in the front yard.Some pieces are made individually, while others bring together their different artistic approaches through collaboration.The artists have shaped their living space around what makes them happy, believing they should be free to create an environment they enjoy without worrying about conventional ideas of how a home should look.Carol Sackman holds a Master of Fine Arts and a Bachelor of Fine Arts from the Maryland Institute, College of Art. She has previously taught art classes and now works professionally across painting, sculpture, fabric work, and mosaics.She draws inspiration from discarded objects, often taking apart computer circuit boards and watch parts to create unexpected combinations. She enjoys experimenting with these materials and says the process can be just as exciting as the finished artwork, with each piece becoming a new adventure. Visitors to the artists’ mosaic-covered home also bring their own reactions, which Sackman says can vary widely. After visiting the home, some people even bring discarded objects for the artists to use in their future mosaics.White is a self-taught artist who initially explored stained glass before discovering his passion for mosaics. He began working on the house's mosaic designs in 2003 and has continued developing his practice for more than 20 years.He developed his skills by experimenting with materials found at yard sales, thrift shops, and through donations. The artist later acquired kilns, allowing them to make additional objects for their mosaics. White draws inspiration from art environments created by other artists.One prominent influence is the religious grotto in Dickeyville, Wisconsin. He also values the way people respond to their work. White says seeing people experience happiness through the mosaics is one of the things he enjoys most about creating them.For Sackman and White, their home reflects the creative freedom they value in their everyday lives. They produce some artworks together and others individually, respecting their different approaches to making art. Both believe creativity should be open to everyone and that people should continue to play, experiment and explore new ideas as adults.Their work combines materials such as paint, fabric and broken objects, giving these items new life through mosaics and other art forms. Sackman enjoys bringing unexpected objects together, while White continues to develop his skills by experimenting with different materials. Through their mosaic-covered home, the artists hope to inspire visitors to embrace their own creativity and shape their surroundings in ways that make them happy.
Article Summary: Carol Sackman and Blake White purchased the house in 2000 and began decorating it with mosaics in 2003. Over the years, their artwork has spread across much of the kitchen, bathrooms, back garden fence and the sides of the house. Their work combines materials such as paint, fabric and broken objects, giving these items new life through mosaics.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.
Article Summary: Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.

Article Title: Microsoft announces Maia 300, CEO Satya Nadella calls it ‘biggest bet yet on our own silicon’
Article Text:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella calls ‘Maia 300’ company’s biggest bet on silicon

Today we are announcing our biggest bet yet on our own silicon.

Starting next calendar year, we will scale our Maia family to multi-gigawatt deployments, making it the primary inference system for our own product and services.

And we’re introducing Maia 300, which delivers 40% more tokens per watt compared to leading GPU-based systems.

We are already deploying Maia 200 across the US, Europe, and Australia, delivering up to 1.7x more tokens per watt across experiences in Teams and Copilot.

Our goal is to build on the full-stack efficiency gains we’ve already seen, while continuing to bring the latest innovations from across the ecosystem into our fleet.

Hardware gains: Density and energy efficiency

Microsoft has announced its third-generation custom artificial intelligence (AI) chip and inference platform, the Maia 300, marking an aggressive push to run more of its AI infrastructure on homegrown hardware after years of heavy reliance on Nvidia’s market-dominant processors. Executive leadership described the rollout as the company’s “biggest bet yet on our own silicon,” positioning the processor as the future operational backbone for its consumer, developer, and enterprise services. Production of the Maia 300 is scheduled to begin in 2027, and Microsoft plans to use the platform as its primary inference engine to process incoming AI queries across its ecosystem, powering tools such as Copilot, Microsoft Teams, GitHub, Foundry and Dragon Copilot.Engineered specifically for complex modern computing, including advanced reasoning, conversational bots and autonomous agentic workflows, the Maia 300 introduces notable efficiency and density leaps over its predecessors.Microsoft plans to install 96 Maia 300 chips into every server rack, effectively doubling the 48-chip density of the Maia 200. The platform achieves up to seven times higher token throughput per rack compared to the Maia 200. Moreover, the hardware is claimed to produce 40% more tokens per megawatt, delivering notable power savings compared to standard GPUs.While Nvidia graphics processing units remain the default industry standard for model training and fill Microsoft’s existing cloud data centers, high market demand and soaring infrastructure costs have pushed major cloud providers toward hardware diversification.Looking ahead, Microsoft plans to scale Azure Maia platforms across multi-gigawatt deployments starting in 2027, according to an announcement from Executive Vice President Scott Guthrie. General Manager Alistair Speirs declined to provide a more specific timeline for the broader gigawatt expansion, but the trajectory signals Microsoft's clear intent to control its own hardware fate as enterprise AI demand accelerates.
Article Summary: Microsoft has announced its third-generation custom artificial intelligence (AI) chip and inference platform, the Maia 300. Executive leadership described the rollout as the company’s “biggest bet yet on our own silicon,” positioning the processor as the future operational backbone for its consumer, developer, and enterprise services. Microsoft plans to scale Azure Maia platforms across multi- gigawatt deployments starting in 2027.

Article Title: Why Google DeepMind is watermarking ‘Biology’
Article Text:
Google DeepMind SynthID Bio

What is SynthID Bio Google DeepMind introduced

What is Biosecurity

AI can create designs that slip past the usual checks used when DNA is ordered from a lab.

3D structures that are wrongly labelled as real can pollute public scientific databases and mislead the research that builds on them.

How SynthID Bio watermark works

Google DeepMind, Google ’s AI lab, recently introduced a technology called SynthID Bio that essentially puts a hidden watermark on proteins designed by artificial intelligence (AI). The main motive of this is that anyone can later check where a design came from, serving as a key security measure in strengthening biosecurity. Moreover, this tech will also serve a way to mitigate the risk of mislabeled synthetic 3D structures polluting public databases and misleading downstream research. The key point is that the watermark doesn’t get in the way of how the protein works.Sarah Carter, a biosecurity policy expert and Principal at Science Policy Consulting who reviewed the work, called it “an important piece of the puzzle for tracking the provenance of biological designs.” She said that by linking designs to the model developer, the watermarks “empower developers to lead on safety and allow synthesis providers to streamline screening for customers who have used those models.” SynthID Bio is currently available as a research release, with open-source code and data made accessible to the scientific community.You may know watermarks from photos or documents, where a faint mark shows who made something.If you are an AI model user and follow news closely, tech companies have introduced watermarking AI-generated content with Google bringing its own version SynthID that serves as an invisible marker for photos, videos, audio and text created by AI. SynthID Bio does something similar for biology. It hides a signature inside AI-generated protein designs, including the written sequences and the predicted 3D shapes.The signature can’t be seen but it can be verified. It works on the digital model and it also works on the actual protein once it has been made in a lab. According to Google, in laboratory tests, the watermarked designs matched the performance and natural variety of designs without a watermark.According to Scientific Journal ScienceDirect, Biosecurity is a combination of practices and protocols designed to prevent the transmission of harmful biological agents, infectious diseases and invasive species like viruses and bacteria.The COVID-19 pandemic is one great example of biosecurity. As per an article on National Library of Medicine (National Center for Biotechnology Information), “the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic is a stark reminder of the devastation biological threats can cause.”The “global community saw a massive surge in the demand for diagnostic capacities, which had a substantial impact on biosafety and biosecurity. Laboratories had to cope with a surge in laboratory testing capacity, while resources and training possibilities were limited. In addition, the pandemic highlighted the impact biological threats can have, thereby giving rise to new dialogue about biosecurity and new biological threats. ”The paper published in the Journal highlighted issues regarding biosafety and biosecurity during the pandemic, and recommended improvement in future biosafety and biosecurity to increase preparedness for the next global health crisis.This also answers the question, “Why this matters now?” AI is already helping scientists with some of biology’s hardest problems: it can predict the structure of proteins (AlphaFold) and design brand-new ones (AlphaProteo and ProteinMPNN). More recently it has been used to develop new bacteriophages, which are viruses that infect bacteria.But these tools also bring new risks, and DeepMind points to two:SynthID Bio is not a single method. It is a family of methods, and each one is matched to the type of data being marked. For protein sequences, it gently steers which amino acids are chosen while for predicted 3D structures, it slightly adjusts the atomic coordinates.Together, these small changes create a reliable signal that can be detected later. In experiments, they did not damage the protein’s biological function, which matters if the proteins are going to be used to treat disease or support research.DeepMind compares biosecurity to a “Swiss cheese” defence. Every safeguard, such as model-level protections or vetting customers, has some gaps. Stack several together and each one covers the holes in the others. SynthID Bio adds another layer, built into the biological design itself.In the past, a DNA sequence that looked unfamiliar could safely be assumed to come from some undiscovered natural organism. That assumption no longer holds, because AI can create entirely new sequences that look nothing like known hazards. Checking that an unfamiliar order isn’t an engineered threat takes lengthy manual reviews, which can hold up important research.This is where SynthID Bio can help. It gives screeners an automated signal showing that an order came from a trusted model with built-in safeguards.
Article Summary: Google DeepMind introduced a technology called SynthID Bio that essentially puts a hidden watermark on proteins designed by artificial intelligence. The main motive of this is that anyone can later check where a design came from, serving as a key security measure in strengthening biosecurity. This tech will also serve a way to mitigate the risk of mislabeled synthetic 3D structures polluting public databases.

Article Title: Google DeepMind is hiring AI engineers for its new team with salary of up to $1.1 million, no degree required; all the company wants is...
Article Text:
Google DeepMind is hiring for Polaris.

Every Polaris test for Gemini takes about a week to build

A very good vibe coder can land the Google DeepMind job

Google DeepMind is hiring engineers for Polaris, a new team that builds tests to measure how well Gemini handles real software engineering work. The pay stands out. Total compensation runs from $550,000 to $1.1 million a year, and you don’t need a degree to apply.Tamay Besiroglu, an Epoch AI co-founder who now works on data at Google DeepMind, kept the brief simple in a post on X. “All we care about is you being smart and able to solve hard problems,” he wrote, adding that people should ignore the pay mentioned in the job ad. When asked whether the listing was wrong, he clarified that its numbers were accurate but left out equity. The base salary alone sits between $164,000 and $252,000.The role, listed as Research Engineer and based in Mountain View, California, centres on designing tasks. Each one is a detailed exam for Gemini, made up of a prompt telling the model what to do and a grader or rubric that scores its attempt.Instead of producing tests in bulk through a synthetic data pipeline, Polaris engineers hand-build a smaller set that captures the complexity of real-world coding. A single task usually takes about a week, from first idea to final approval.Engineers will also start new projects to improve Gemini’s training data and evaluations. Google first called for Polaris applicants on September 25, describing it as a new DeepMind team designing evaluation frameworks for AI coding agents.On paper, the minimum bar asks for software development experience and hands-on use of AI coding tools and developer agents. A track record at contests like the IMO, Putnam or IOI, or experience designing benchmarks and evaluation rubrics, counts in your favour.Besiroglu’s replies on X widened the door further. Asked if non-engineers could apply, he said quick learners were fine. Asked about vibe coders, he said they just need to be very good ones. He also confirmed the team doesn’t ask LeetCode questions. When one user called Google’s hiring process “laughably bad”, Besiroglu said his own team runs the interviews and that he thinks the process is good.So what is DeepMind looking for in an engineer? Someone smart who can solve hard problems, Besiroglu said. Experience with AI coding agents, he added, is very useful too.
Article Summary: Google DeepMind is hiring engineers for Polaris, a new team that builds tests to measure how well Gemini handles real software engineering work. Total compensation runs from $550,000 to $1.1 million a year, and you don’t need a degree to apply.

The workshop, developed with artist Arushi Kathuria, will run from 14 October to 9 November and will be offered in select locations across the United States, Canada, Malaysia and Singapore in addition to India.Alongside the Special Edition AirPods launch, Apple has rolled out a range of festive shopping benefits and services through its online and retail channels:* Up to 12 months of No Cost EMI on selected products, plus instant cashback of up to Rs 15,000 with eligible cards.* Free engraving on eligible products including AirPods, iPad, AirTag and Apple Pencil, allowing customers to personalise gifts with names, initials, numbers or emoji.* Special Edition AirPods 5 with festive engraving, available exclusively through Apple retail channels.* Custom Mac configurations, available directly through Apple.* Personalised shopping experience through the Apple Store app.* Complimentary setup assistance from Apple Specialists for new device owners.* Trade-in offers, with customers able to receive between Rs 4,500 and Rs 81,500 in credit when exchanging eligible smartphones. Trade-ins for Macs, iPads and Apple Watches are also available.* Digital gift messaging through the Apple Store app, allowing customers to send personalised festive greetings with purchases.* Three months of Apple Music free with the purchase of eligible Apple devices.* Free today (October 12) at Apple festive workshops, including the Rangoli drawing session on iPad using Procreate.* Interactive Rangoli wallpaper creator, enabling customers to design, download and share personalised festive artwork.

Article Title: Experts say AI may change the price of food and groceries: What is good and bad for customers
Article Text:
How AI is entering the grocery aisles and popular food chains

What experts say about dynamic pricing

What is good and bad for shoppers

Food retailers are rapidly adopting artificial intelligence (AI) to run their operations. While the technology promises inventory efficiency and targeted discounts, economists and legal scholars warn it could also usher in an era of personalised and dynamic pricing – fundamentally altering what shoppers pay for everyday essentials.According to CNBC, retailers worldwide are testing and expanding data-driven systems at multiple touchpoints. US grocer Kroger introduced FlashFood, an AI platform that spots perishable items nearing their expiration dates, reduces their prices, and notifies shoppers via an app. Major chains in the US, including Kroger, Walmart, Whole Foods and Amazon Fresh are also rolling out digital screens to replace paper price tags, as are UK grocers Tesco, Morrisons and Asda. These digital tags enable stores to update shelf prices remotely in seconds.Financial platform Revolut recently tested facial-recognition checkouts at select coffee shops, letting buyers pay with a glance. In the UK, Sainsbury’s launched “SmartLists,” an AI tool that converts photos or meal ideas into curated shopping lists.Recently, an antitrust lawsuit accused McDonald’s of using an AI-driven “pricing engine” to determine menu rates across US stores and allegedly overcharge customers for staples like Big Macs and french fries.McDonald’s denied using AI to calculate what individual customers are willing to spend, asserting that it merely offers franchisees "tools, resources, research and recommendations to help them make informed decisions. "As automated infrastructure expands, experts caution that retailers have the tools to adjust pricing in real time based on demand patterns.“Dynamic pricing means changing prices in response to changing market conditions, such as demand, timing, capacity or competitors’ prices. It is not new. Airlines, hotels, and ride-hailing services have used it for years,” Miroslava Marinova, senior lecturer of commercial law at the University of East London, was quoted as saying.However, the rapid collection of granular personal data, which includes purchase records, browsing history, device location and buying routines, is beginning to blur the lines between broad market shifts and personal profiles.“Dynamic pricing responds primarily to market conditions, whereas personalised pricing uses information about the consumer to estimate willingness to pay. As retailers combine market-level information with increasingly detailed consumer data, the boundary between dynamic and personalised pricing becomes thinner,” Marinova explained.Algorithmic pricing is not inherently harmful to household budgets, the report said. Algorithms can lower prices on overstocked or aging inventory, curbing food waste and offering cheaper options for budget-conscious buyers. As a result, when discounts are applied strategically, certain foods and grocery services become more accessible to lower-income segments.However, there are some risks involved. The downside of individual-level pricing models centers on transparency and market fairness. When prices fluctuate continuously, shoppers cannot tell whether a price tag reflects general market supply or their personal browsing profile.“If consumers cannot understand why they received a particular price, cannot compare it with prices offered to others, and cannot effectively switch to another supplier, the normal disciplining effect of consumer choice becomes weaker,” Marinova warned.The Bank of England economists pointed out that when prices change constantly and differently for every shopper, measuring inflation becomes difficult.
Article Summary: Food retailers are rapidly adopting artificial intelligence (AI) to run their operations. While the technology promises inventory efficiency and targeted discounts, economists and legal scholars warn it could usher in an era of personalised and dynamic pricing. Algorithms can lower prices on overstocked or aging inventory, curbing food waste and offering cheaper options for budget- conscious buyers.
